title: Iran Knowledge Atlas
scope: Public research showcase. Historical descriptions and selected model outputs are published; research implementation and parameterization remain private.

researchLayers.label: Evidence
researchLayers.description: Documented events, people, institutions, places and source links, with explicit citation status.

researchLayers.label: Reconstruction
researchLayers.description: Normalized historical model outputs conditional on proxy coding and uncalibrated assumptions; not observations.

researchLayers.label: Simulation
researchLayers.description: Named forward experiments generated by the private System Dynamics engine and published only as outputs.

events.title: Median political consolidation
events.detail: The Medes emerge as a major plateau power, though the chronology and structure remain disputed.

events.title: Defeat by Cyrus II
events.detail: Median political authority is absorbed into the new Achaemenid state.

events.title: Achaemenid state founded
events.detail: Cyrus II defeats Astyages and begins a durable imperial administration.

events.title: Royal Road system
events.detail: Roads and relay stations lower the cost of moving information, officials and goods.

events.title: Macedonian conquest
events.detail: The Achaemenid state collapses after Alexander's invasion.

events.title: Seleucid imperial foundation
events.detail: A Hellenistic successor state links Iranian territories to Mediterranean urban networks.

events.title: Arsacid revolt
events.detail: Parthian power begins to displace Seleucid control in the east.

events.title: Parthian capture of Mesopotamia
events.detail: Control of Mesopotamian corridors strengthens the empire's Eurasian position.

events.title: Roman–Parthian war cycle
events.detail: Repeated frontier wars impose losses without ending long-distance exchange.

events.title: Sasanian overthrow
events.detail: Ardashir defeats the last Arsacid king and founds a new centralized empire.

events.title: Gondishapur scholarly complex
events.detail: Medical and philosophical traditions cluster around Gondishapur; its exact form is debated.

events.title: Last Roman–Persian war
events.detail: Decades of total war exhaust both empires before the Arab conquests.

events.title: End of Sasanian state
events.detail: Conquest and regime transition dismantle the imperial order.

events.title: Abbasid Revolution
events.detail: Strong Iranian participation shifts the caliphal center eastward and enlarges scholarly exchange.

events.title: Translation and calculation networks
events.detail: Iranian-origin scholars participate in the mathematical, astronomical and translation movements.

events.title: Tahirid autonomy
events.detail: Hereditary regional rule marks a new phase of Iranian political autonomy.

events.title: Saffarid rise
events.detail: A new eastern dynasty expands from Sistan and challenges older elites.

events.title: New Persian court culture
events.detail: Persian gains renewed standing in courtly and literary life.

events.title: Samanid cultural apex
events.detail: Bukhara becomes a major center of New Persian literature, libraries and scholarship.

events.title: Age of Ibn Sina and al-Biruni
events.detail: Two of the period's greatest polymaths emerge from eastern Iranian scholarly networks.

events.title: Shahnameh completed
events.detail: Ferdowsi completes the great Persian epic, preserving and reshaping Iranian historical memory.

events.title: Medical and philosophical synthesis
events.detail: Major encyclopedic works circulate across Persianate courts and schools.

events.title: Isfahan becomes Seljuk center
events.detail: Political consolidation supports courtly and scholarly infrastructure.

events.title: Nizamiyya institutions
events.detail: Endowed colleges strengthen the reproduction of learned elites.

events.title: Jalali calendar
events.detail: Astronomers associated with Omar Khayyam complete a highly accurate solar calendar reform.

events.title: Khwarazmian expansion
events.detail: A broad commercial empire forms across Iran and Central Asia.

events.title: Otrar crisis
events.detail: The breakdown with Chinggis Khan precedes a catastrophic invasion.

events.title: Mongol invasions
events.detail: Conquest brings severe mortality, urban destruction and displacement.

events.title: Maragheh Observatory
events.detail: A major observatory, library and transregional scholarly network is established.

events.title: Ilkhanid administrative recovery
events.detail: Reforms and conversion under Ghazan support a more stable fiscal and cultural order.

events.title: Fragmented successor states
events.detail: Competing courts sustain culture while warfare weakens long-term institutional accumulation.

events.title: Hafez's Shiraz
events.detail: Shiraz remains a major literary center despite political instability.

events.title: Herat renaissance
events.detail: Timurid courts support art, architecture, literature and science after the first conquest wave.

events.title: Samarkand Observatory
events.detail: Ulugh Beg's institution supports precise astronomical observations and tables.

events.title: Turkmen court networks
events.detail: Aq Qoyunlu and Qara Qoyunlu courts connect Tabriz, Shiraz and wider diplomatic networks.

events.title: Safavid unification
events.detail: A durable territorial state reconstitutes Iran under a new religious-political order.

events.title: Isfahan becomes capital
events.detail: Investment makes Isfahan a major commercial, architectural and intellectual center.

events.title: Siege and Safavid collapse
events.detail: Invasion, famine and prolonged war severely weaken population and institutions.

events.title: Nader crowned
events.detail: Military consolidation rapidly restores territorial power.

events.title: Campaign in India
events.detail: Imperial expansion brings wealth but entrenches a high-extraction military state.

events.title: Assassination and fragmentation
events.detail: Nader's death triggers renewed succession conflict.

events.title: Shiraz reconstruction
events.detail: Karim Khan's court invests in urban recovery, commerce and architecture.

events.title: Qajar conquest
events.detail: The defeat of Lotf Ali Khan ends Zand rule.

events.title: Dar al-Funun opens
events.detail: A modern polytechnic introduces systematic instruction in medicine, engineering and military sciences.

events.title: Tobacco Protest
events.detail: A national political network demonstrates new forms of public coordination.

events.title: Constitutional Revolution
events.detail: Constitutionalism, newspapers and civic mobilization enlarge the public sphere.

events.title: University of Tehran
events.detail: A national university consolidates modern higher education and research disciplines.

events.title: Literacy Corps
events.detail: A national campaign expands primary education into rural areas.

events.title: Revolution
events.detail: Political transformation remakes universities, administration and the knowledge environment.

events.title: Iran–Iraq War
events.detail: Eight years of war impose mortality, displacement and resource costs.

events.title: Mass university expansion
events.detail: Higher education grows rapidly across regions and among women.

events.title: Internet connection
events.detail: Digital connectivity opens a new channel for global information exchange.

events.title: Intensified sanctions
events.detail: Financial and technology restrictions raise research, trade and mobility costs.

events.title: COVID-19 shock
events.detail: Mortality and school disruption reduce capability while digital adoption accelerates.

events.title: Woman, Life, Freedom
events.detail: A major social rupture reveals civic capability alongside repression and emigration pressure.

scholars.name: Zoroaster
scholars.bio: Attributed founder of the Zoroastrian tradition. His date and association with Median history remain deeply contested, so the atlas treats him as contextual rather than securely dynastic.

scholars.name: Udjahorresnet
scholars.bio: An Egyptian physician and official who served Cambyses and Darius, illustrating how expertise circulated within the Achaemenid imperial network.

scholars.name: Democedes
scholars.bio: A Greek physician described by Herodotus as practicing at Darius I's court; evidence concerns the empire's cosmopolitan knowledge network, not Persian ethnicity.

scholars.name: Berossus
scholars.bio: A Babylonian priest who wrote a Greek history of Babylonia under Seleucid rule, bridging Mesopotamian records and Hellenistic scholarship.

scholars.name: Seleucus of Seleucia
scholars.bio: An astronomer from Seleucia known for defending heliocentric ideas and studying tides within the Hellenistic Iranian-Mesopotamian sphere.

scholars.name: Bardaisan
scholars.bio: A Syriac intellectual from Edessa under Arsacid influence who wrote on philosophy, religion and natural phenomena.

scholars.name: Mani
scholars.bio: Born in Parthian Mesopotamia, Mani developed a universalist religious-philosophical system that spread across Eurasia.

scholars.name: Borzuya
scholars.bio: Physician under Khosrow I associated with translating the Panchatantra into Middle Persian, an emblem of cross-cultural knowledge transfer.

scholars.name: Paul the Persian
scholars.bio: A philosopher linked to the Sasanian court who composed works on Aristotelian logic and philosophy in Syriac.

scholars.name: Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ
scholars.bio: Iranian-born prose writer who translated Middle Persian works into Arabic and shaped Arabic political and literary prose.

scholars.name: al-Khwarizmi
scholars.bio: Scholar of Khwarazmian origin whose works on algebra and calculation transformed mathematics across Eurasia.

scholars.name: Hanzala Badghisi
scholars.bio: Among the earliest recorded poets of New Persian, representing the language's re-emergence as a literary medium.

scholars.name: al-Razi
scholars.bio: Rayy-born physician whose clinical and pharmacological compilations profoundly influenced medicine in Arabic, Persian and Latin traditions.

scholars.name: al-Biruni
scholars.bio: Mathematician, astronomer, geographer and historian of religions renowned for measurement and comparative inquiry.

scholars.name: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
scholars.bio: Author of the Canon of Medicine and a vast philosophical system that shaped Islamic and European intellectual history.

scholars.name: Ferdowsi
scholars.bio: Author of the Shahnameh, the monumental Persian epic that preserved and reimagined Iran's pre-Islamic historical memory.

scholars.name: Omar Khayyam
scholars.bio: Nishapur polymath who classified cubic equations and contributed to the Jalali calendar as well as philosophy and poetry.

scholars.name: al-Ghazali
scholars.bio: Tus-born thinker whose critique and synthesis of philosophy, theology and ethics influenced Islamic thought for centuries.

scholars.name: Suhrawardi
scholars.bio: Iranian philosopher who founded the Illuminationist school, combining rigorous argument with a metaphysics of light.

scholars.name: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi
scholars.bio: Rayy-born encyclopedic thinker whose works ranged across theology, philosophy, medicine and natural inquiry.

scholars.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
scholars.bio: Polymath and organizer of Maragheh Observatory who advanced trigonometry, astronomy, logic and ethics.

scholars.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
scholars.bio: Physician, philosopher and astronomer trained at Maragheh who contributed to optics and planetary theory.

scholars.name: Hafez
scholars.bio: Shiraz poet whose compressed, multivalent ghazals became foundational to Persian literary and intellectual culture.

scholars.name: Jamshid al-Kashi
scholars.bio: A leading mathematician at Samarkand who calculated π with exceptional precision and advanced decimal computation.

scholars.name: Ulugh Beg
scholars.bio: Timurid ruler and astronomer whose Samarkand observatory produced one of the finest pre-telescopic star catalogues.

scholars.name: Mulla Sadra
scholars.bio: Major philosopher of the School of Isfahan whose Transcendent Philosophy synthesized Avicennism, illumination and theology.

scholars.name: Mir Damad
scholars.bio: Central Isfahan thinker who developed the concept of origination in perpetuity and trained Mulla Sadra.

scholars.name: Hazin Lahiji
scholars.bio: A philosopher, historian and poet whose migrations after Safavid collapse document the era's intellectual displacement.

scholars.name: Mohammad Mahdi Naraqi
scholars.bio: Scholar of ethics, philosophy, mathematics and astronomy active across the Afsharid-Zand transition.

scholars.name: Amir Kabir
scholars.bio: Reforming statesman who founded Dar al-Funun, sponsored translation and sought administrative and technical modernization.

scholars.name: Mirza Malkom Khan
scholars.bio: Writer and reform advocate who circulated constitutional, legal and administrative ideas through newspapers and diplomacy.

scholars.name: Lotfi A. Zadeh
scholars.bio: University of Tehran graduate and Berkeley professor who created fuzzy-set theory, a foundation for reasoning with imprecision.

scholars.name: Ehsan Yarshater
scholars.bio: Iranian scholar who founded Encyclopaedia Iranica and built enduring institutions for the academic study of Iranian civilization.

scholars.name: Maryam Mirzakhani
scholars.bio: Sharif graduate and Stanford professor whose work on geometry and dynamical systems earned the 2014 Fields Medal—the first awarded to a woman.

scholars.name: Nima Arkani-Hamed
scholars.bio: Leading particle theorist known for new approaches to hierarchy problems, extra dimensions and scattering amplitudes.

scholars.name: Abdolkarim Soroush
scholars.bio: Iranian philosopher of religion and political thought known for arguments about religious knowledge, pluralism and reform.
